blueprint_concepts: Linear combination theorem in a plane
english: Let $OABC$ be a tetrahedron, and let $\overrightarrow{a}$, $\overrightarrow{b}$, $\overrightarrow{c}$ be the position vectors of $A$, $B$, $C$, respectively, with respect to $O$. Let $D$ be the point on the side $BC$ with $BD:DC=2:1$, let $E$ be the point on the side $CA$ with $CE:EA=1:2$, and let $G$ be the point of intersection of the lines $AD$ and $BE$. Let $M$ be the mid-point of $OA$. The line $MG$ meets the plane $OBC$ at the point $P$, and $\overrightarrow{OP}=p\,\overrightarrow{b}+q\,\overrightarrow{c}$. Then the value of $p-q$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $OABC$ एक चतुष्फलक है, तथा $\overrightarrow{a}$, $\overrightarrow{b}$, $\overrightarrow{c}$ क्रमशः $A$, $B$, $C$ के $O$ के सापेक्ष स्थिति सदिश हैं। माना कि $D$ भुजा $BC$ पर वह बिन्दु है जिसके लिए $BD:DC=2:1$ है, $E$ भुजा $CA$ पर वह बिन्दु है जिसके लिए $CE:EA=1:2$ है, तथा $G$ रेखाओं $AD$ और $BE$ का प्रतिच्छेदन बिन्दु है। माना कि $M$, $OA$ का मध्य-बिन्दु है। रेखा $MG$ तल $OBC$ से बिन्दु $P$ पर मिलती है, तथा $\overrightarrow{OP}=p\,\overrightarrow{b}+q\,\overrightarrow{c}$ है। तब $p-q$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Line $MG$: $\dfrac12\overrightarrow{a}+k\left(\overrightarrow{OG}-\dfrac12\overrightarrow{a}\right)$; in plane $OBC$ the coefficient of $\overrightarrow{a}$ is $0$: $\dfrac12-\dfrac{k}{4}=0\Rightarrow k=2$
solution_full: By the section formula, $D$ divides $BC$ in the ratio $2:1$, so $\overrightarrow{OD}=\dfrac{1\cdot\overrightarrow{b}+2\overrightarrow{c}}{3}$; $E$ divides $CA$ in the ratio $1:2$, so $\overrightarrow{OE}=\dfrac{2\overrightarrow{c}+1\cdot\overrightarrow{a}}{3}$.

In the plane $ABC$ the lines $AD$ and $BE$ meet at one point $G$. A point of $AD$ is $\overrightarrow{a}+s(\overrightarrow{OD}-\overrightarrow{a})=(1-s)\overrightarrow{a}+\dfrac{s}{3}\overrightarrow{b}+\dfrac{2s}{3}\overrightarrow{c}$.

Since $\overrightarrow{a},\overrightarrow{b},\overrightarrow{c}$ are non-coplanar, a vector has only one expression in terms of them, so the coefficients are equal: $\dfrac{2s}{3}=\dfrac{2t}{3}$, $1-s=\dfrac{t}{3}$, $\dfrac{s}{3}=1-t$.
From the first, $s=t$; then $1-s=\dfrac{s}{3}$ gives $s=\dfrac34$, and the third equation also holds.
So $\overrightarrow{OG}=\dfrac14\overrightarrow{a}+\dfrac14\overrightarrow{b}+\dfrac12\overrightarrow{c}$ (the coefficients add to $1$, as they must for a point of plane $ABC$).

A point lies in the plane $OBC$ exactly when it is a combination of $\overrightarrow{b}$ and $\overrightarrow{c}$ alone, that is when the coefficient of $\overrightarrow{a}$ is $0$ (again by uniqueness): $\dfrac12-\dfrac{k}{4}=0$, $k=2$.
originality_note: New: a point fixed by two cevians in a face of a tetrahedron is projected from the mid-point of an edge onto the opposite face; both steps are coefficient matching, once in the plane ABC and once in space (way 5). Closest known: intersection of two cevians of a triangle by vectors; centroid of a tetrahedron. Different because: the second line leaves the face and its trace on plane OBC is read from the vanishing coefficient of a.

concept_use.Linear combination theorem in space: Uniqueness of coefficients of a, b, c gives s = t = 3/4 for G, and the condition 'coefficient of a = 0' for P in plane OBC.
concept_use.Linear combination theorem in a plane: Points of the lines AD and BE in the plane ABC are written as combinations of A and D, B and E (coefficients adding to 1) to locate G.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol and object is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath, is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Checked the ratio directions (D nearer C, E nearer C) with explicit vectors; P exists since the a-coefficient changes along MG. Changed: No change.
key_step: Matching coefficients twice: the cevian intersection G in face ABC, then the a-coefficient of the line MG.
justification: Two linked uses of linear combination (plane then space) with section formula; a slip in ratio direction gives a wrong value and the format is numerical. Like 2025-P1-Q9 (L4) in mass-point flavour but more routine, so L3; similar to 2023-P2-Q4 (L1) plus two more stages.
